frames.transcript_context:
In case of big concrete construction projects like bridges, steel reinforcement bars alone
won't be sufficient to provide the necessary tensile strength.
In this case, pre-stressed concrete is being used.
In pre-stressing, the rods or tendons are stretched along the axis and cement is poured.
Later when the tendons are released the compression is generated at the bottom, which tries to
counterbalance the compression due to loading at the top part of the beam.
The principle behind pre-stressed concrete is that compressive stresses induced by the
high strength steel tendons in a concrete member before loads are applied. This will
balance the stresses imposed in the member during the service.

limitations: Useful coverage for every assigned lecture, not exhaustive every visual/spoken step.
Change scoring compares bounded samples; brief changes between samples can be missed.
Raw Small English ASR context and OCR preserved; no technical wording rewrite or equation certification.
Small text and cropped scrolling boundaries can limit readability.
Final manifest includes only retained images; rejected PNG derivatives remain for reproducibility but are not selected references.

report.ocr: Tesseract sparse-text OCR, raw output preserved.
report.transcript_context: Raw SRT cues intersecting +/-25 seconds around measured capture timestamp.
limitations: Sampling may miss brief intermediate writing or fast dialog changes.
ASR topic labels and context are uncorrected evidence and can contain technical substitutions.
Embedded video clips retained only where they illustrate lecture content; meeting recursion and blank/dialog occlusion rejected.
